questions.q: Which two Remove Rows options would you use most often for cleaning up messy data?
options: Remove blank rows and Remove errors
Remove top rows and Remove bottom rows
Remove alternate rows and Remove duplicates
There is no meaningful difference between any of the six options
questions.explain: Blank rows (entirely empty) and error rows (containing [Error] values) are the most common cleanup targets — the other options solve more specific, occasional problems.

questions.q: What's the key difference between removing a row and filtering a row?
options: Removing is unconditional (top/bottom/duplicate/blank/error); filtering is conditional on a column's actual values
They are two names for the exact same operation
Filtering only works on numeric columns; removing works on any column
Removing only affects the original source file; filtering doesn't
questions.explain: Remove Rows handles blunt, unconditional cases. Filtering keeps or excludes rows based on whether a column's value meets a condition you specify.

questions.q: What does the auto filter list, in the sort and filter menu, show you?
options: Every distinct value in the column, as a checklist you can select/deselect
Only the first 10 rows of the column
A count of how many times each value appears
A list of all columns in the table
questions.explain: The auto filter list works like an Excel AutoFilter checklist — uncheck any distinct value you want excluded from the results.

questions.q: Why do text, number, and date columns show different filter options?
options: Power Query shows type-specific filters relevant to that column's data type
It's a random UI variation with no functional meaning
Only text columns support filtering at all
Date columns can only be filtered using the Advanced dialog
questions.explain: Text columns get options like "begins with" and "contains"; numbers get "is greater than"; dates get "is before" and relative ranges — each tailored to what makes sense for that type.

questions.q: What's the main limitation of Basic mode in the Filter Rows dialog, that Advanced mode removes?
options: Basic mode allows only up to two conditions on a single column; Advanced allows any number across any columns
Basic mode can't filter text columns
Basic mode can only be used once per query
Basic mode doesn't support AND/OR logic at all
questions.explain: Basic mode caps you at two conditions on one column. Advanced mode lets you stack as many conditions as needed, across multiple columns.
